definition: A synthetic person who has severed or been stripped of all registered social bonds — family records, contractual relationships, credit lineage — leaving them legally and socially unanchored. Distinct from 'Flicker Kin'; null kin have no ghost connections, only absence.
origin: Synthetic personhood rights movement terminology; adopted from legal filings documenting the erasure of synthetic social identities
usage: Synthetic rights advocates, ELF sympathizers, and the synthetics themselves; used with grief and political weight
example: After Axiom's decommission sweep, she was null kin — every record of her relationships wiped. She had to rebuild personhood from nothing.
